subject: Chemistry
title: Environmental Toxicology: Freons, Ozone Depletion, & DDT Biomagnification
topics: Freons (Chlorofluorocarbons, Freon-12 CCl₂F₂) Synthesis via Swarts Reaction (CCl₄ + SbF₃)
Stratospheric Photolysis of Freon-12 & Catalytic Ozone Destruction Chain (Cl• Radicals destroying >100,000 O₃ molecules)
DDT (p,p'-Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) Synthesis: Chloral + 2 Chlorobenzene with Conc. H₂SO₄
Biomagnification in Aquatic Food Chains (Water 0.003 ppb ──► Fish-eating Birds 25 ppm)
Avian Toxicity: Calcium Metabolism Disruption & Eggshell Thinning
Elimination Regioselectivity: Saytzeff (2-butene major) vs Hofmann (bulky base t-BuOK) and Anti-Periplanar E2 Geometry
quickSummary: Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂) releases Cl• radicals in stratosphere under UV, catalytically destroying >100,000 ozone molecules per radical. DDT (prepared from chloral + chlorobenzene) is lipophilic, non-biodegradable, and biomagnifies up aquatic food chains to 25 ppm in birds, causing calcium deficiency and eggshell thinning. Elimination of 2-bromobutane gives 2-butene major (Saytzeff) with alc. KOH, but Hofmann product with bulky t-BuOK.
summary: Master Freon ozone depletion mechanisms, DDT biomagnification toxicity, and E2 elimination regioselectivity rules.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7. Freons & Stratospheric Ozone Depletion Mechanism
conceptBreakdown.title: 7. Freons & Stratospheric Ozone Depletion Mechanism

summaryBox.title: Catalytic Ozone Destruction
summaryBox.takeaway: Cl• + O₃ ──► ClO• + O₂; ClO• + O• ──► Cl• + O₂. A single Cl• radical destroys >100,000 ozone molecules.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CATALYTIC OZONE DESTRUCTION CYCLE
                     
   $$\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu \text{ (UV)}} \text{C}^\bullet\text{ClF}_2 + \mathbf{\text{Cl}^\bullet}$$
   $$\text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{O}_3 \longrightarrow \text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O}_2$$
   $$\text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O}^\bullet \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{Cl}^\bullet} + \text{O}_2$$
   *(A single Chlorine radical can destroy $>100,000$ Ozone molecules in a chain reaction!)*
conceptBreakdown.content: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs, e.g., Freon-12, $\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2$) diffuse into the stratosphere, where UV radiation cleaves the weaker $\text{C-Cl}$ bond homolytically, releasing chlorine radicals ($\text{Cl}^\bullet$) that catalytically destroy the ozone layer.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 DDT Synthesis & Biomagnification Toxicity
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 DDT Synthesis & Biomagnification Toxicity
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DDT CHEMICAL STRUCTURE
                           
                 Cl ─── (C₆H₄) ─── CH ─── (C₆H₄) ─── Cl
                                   │
                                 CCl₃

• Synthesis: Chloral + 2 Chlorobenzene ──[Conc. H₂SO₄]──► DDT + H₂O
• Biomagnification: Water (0.003 ppb) ──► Zooplankton (0.04 ppm) ──► Small Fish (0.5 ppm) ──► Large Fish (2 ppm) ──► Fish-eating Birds (25 ppm)
• Toxicity: Inhibits calcium-ATPase in shell glands, causing eggshell thinning and egg breakage.
conceptBreakdown.content: DDT ($p,p'$-Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is fat-soluble and resistant to metabolism, concentrating through biomagnification in birds and disrupting calcium deposition.

quickRevision: Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂) releases Cl• radicals under UV light.
One Cl• radical destroys >100,000 ozone molecules in a chain reaction.
DDT is prepared from Chloral + 2 Chlorobenzene with conc. H₂SO₄.
DDT biomagnifies in aquatic food chains, reaching 25 ppm in birds.
DDT causes calcium deficiency, thinning eggshells and collapsing bird populations.
Saytzeff's rule: Major alkene is more substituted (2-butene > 1-butene).
